reason: The root bed needs fired granules, so heating the graded regolith seems like the first preparation.
expectation: The kiln will turn the regolith into mineral granules that still need washing.

alternatives.reason: Mixing nutrient solution also serves the roots, but I want to prepare the bed first.

effect: The kiln produced porous granules, so washing them is the next step toward a clean bed.
reaction: The porosity makes the connection to air around roots clearer.
reason: Water should wash the granules before they go around roots.
expectation: The granules will be washed, perhaps leaving a solution to test for salts.

alternatives.reason: The nutrient mix is also needed, but the granules still need cleaning.

effect: The granules are washed, and the test cell is now available to check them.
reaction: A straightforward preparation; I am curious what the test checks.
reason: Test the washed granules before using them as a root bed.
expectation: The cell will check whether undesirable soluble material still leaches from the granules.

effect: The tested granules are ready, and the text distinguishes their support role from nutrients and cabin conditions.
reaction: That division of roles is useful, although I wanted to know the test result more specifically.
reason: Put the clean medium into the prepared troughs.
expectation: The troughs will have a root bed ready for nutrient solution.

alternatives.reason: The solution is also needed, but I want to finish assembling the bed first.

effect: The troughs now contain the mineral bed; they still need water and nutrients.
reaction: A sensible assembly, with no surprise.
reason: Mix the nutrient concentrate into drinking water; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: A measured nutrient solution will be ready for the troughs.

effect: The nutrient solution is ready to add to the bed.
reason: Supply the root troughs with water and nutrients; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: The troughs will be ready to support roots with solution and air between granules.

effect: The irrigated troughs complete the chapter, with circulation inserts and separate places for lettuce and potatoes.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the prepared materials become two specific growing modules, though the inserts appear without an assembly step.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the washed granules and learning that they provide support while imported nutrients and cabin conditions supply other needs gave the construction a clear purpose.

leastWorthwhile.text: Mixing the nutrient solution was a predictable, single available action with little feedback beyond its name.

surprise.text: The finished troughs already included circulation inserts; I had not seen those prepared separately.

arbitrary.text: No choice felt purposeless, but the leach test did not say what it measured or found, so its conclusion felt less informative than I expected.

continue.text: Yes, I would try another chapter to see the lettuce and potatoes grow; this chapter's practical construction was coherent, although most individual steps were predictable.
